title: One Piece’s God Valley Movie Must Make One Major Change to Become a Hit
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! One Piece is going to make history with the upcoming God Valley film. This year’s One Piece Day was a major surprise to fans when the anime confirmed two upcoming films of the series. While the first film is scheduled to be released next year, the other film will premiere in 2029. While all this is going on, the anime is also continuing its yearly schedule ever since the Elbaph Arc began. The manga commenced the arc in September 2024, and the anime followed suit in April this year. For the first time in anime history, One Piece has taken a seasonal schedule to maintain the quality of the animation.

Furthermore, even though a trailer hasn’t been released yet, t he God Valley film is expected to be the best film in One Piece ‘s history . Over the decades, the anime has released 15 feature-length movies and continues to carry on its legacy with more updates. This is the first time in One Piece ‘s history that the anime has ever decided to release a canon movie. So far, every film the anime has released has followed the original script from the animation studio. However, this is all the more reason why expectations for the anime movie are even higher.

One Piece ‘s God Valley Movie Needs to Flesh Out the Fights As Compared to the Manga

The God Valley Incident is easily the best flashback in the series ever. What starts out as Harald’s past, turns into an epic journey that unraveled the biggest mystery behind the incident 38 years ago. However, the fights in the manga pale in comparison to what fans usually get. This is even more disappointing considering that all the legendary figures were present on the island. Instead of focusing on the fights, the story relied more on the lore buildup. However, the movie can turn things around by highlighting the battle scenes in a much better way.

While the backstory introduced the God Valley Incident during the Wano Country Saga, the entire truth wasn’t revealed until years later in the Elbaph Arc of the manga. Not to mention that despite the fact that Kuma’s POV shed some light on the issue, the truth was far more shocking than fans ever realized. The mystery behind the historic incident was finally solved after the introduction of Rocks D. Xebec , a legendary pirate who was at the center of the chaos 38 years ago. Rocks was portrayed as an evil pirate and the instigator behind the incident, but the truth was far from it.

Not only does this flashback depict the true horrors committed by the World Government, but it also reveals how Rocks got entangled in the mess. The backstory revealed the truth behind his lineage and his son, Marshall D. Teach. Apart from the major plot twists, the backstory also includes some of the most intense fights in the series, which makes it all the more worthwhile.

What are your thoughts on the manga fights that took place during the God Valley Incident? Or you can tell us your expectations for the anime movie in the comments below.

title: Classroom of the Elite Season 5 Confirms 2027 Release With First Look Trailer – Watch
content:
Only a few months after the fourth season’s finale, the anime is all set to return next year with a new season. Classroom of the Elite Season 4 aired its final episode in June this year, and while it did have a much longer extended run than previous seasons , it has come to an end with some major teases for the future. Luckily for fans, it was quickly confirmed that Classroom of the Elite Season 5 has been revealed to be in the works following its Season 4 finale. While there are few details about what to expect so far, you can check out the announcement teaser for the next season below.

2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season , which is only a few weeks away, but a lot of the incredible series will be released throughout the year. One of Crunchyroll ‘s biggest anime franchises has confirmed the release date for its new season, and has revealed some huge plans for its premiere. Crunchyroll has a lot of franchises that anime fans will want to check out with the streaming service this year , and fans have already gotten to see a big wave as part of the Winter 2026 anime schedule. As fans gear up for the next wave of new anime coming later this Spring, one of the biggest franchises has now confirmed its release date with some big plans for its first episodes.

Does Classroom of the Elite Season 5 Have a Release Date?

Classroom of the Elite Season 5 has been announced to be in the works, but has yet to confirm a release window or date as of the time of this writing. The potential production staff or returning voice cast have yet to be revealed as of this announcement either, but getting a confirmation of a new season at all is a big show of faith for the anime moving forward. The past two seasons have been developed and released in quick succession compared to the years long wait between the first and second seasons.

Classroom of the Elite had been dormant for five years following the end of the first season, and returned for not only a second season, but a third and fourth as well. Now that a fifth season has been announced, it’s clear that the series is showing no signs of slowing down anytime soon for Kadokawa. That’s especially true as Ayanokoji and the others are now in the midst of their second year in school as of the end of the fourth season.

What to Expect From Classroom of the Elite Season 5

Classroom of the Elite Season 4 ends its adaptation of the first half of the 2nd year for Ayanokoji and the others , and with it introduced a whole new group of rivals that the class now has to deal with in order to make it to the top of the food chain. They had been successful in surviving the first year, but this is an entirely new tier of challenger that even a genius like Ayanokoji has been having to work that much harder to out think and overcome in his schemes so far.

You’re going to need to be sure to catch up with everything now streaming with Crunchyroll in the meantime. Classroom of the Elite is a lot of complicated schemes and tricks that sometimes don’t completely make sense, so you’ll need to pay close attention to the character choices and dialogue in order to keep on top of everything. It seems there might be plenty of time to do so before Season 5.

Are you caught up with all episodes of Classroom of the Elite on Crunchyroll? Head down to the comments to let us know your expectations for Season 5.

title: 6 Years Later, Demon Slayer Star Breaks Silence on Anime’s Most Iconic Moment Ever
content:
Rengoku’s voice actor shares his thoughts on the most iconic anime moment ever. The Demon Slayer : Mugen Train film was released in Japanese theaters on October 16th, 2025, and it made history with its astounding success. Before the anime adaptation was released in 2019, the manga had over 3.5 million copies in circulation, which increased to 10 million in September, around the time of the first season’s finale. The manga continued to rise through the charts, eventually hitting the 100 million milestone about two weeks before Mugen Train ‘s premiere. The series could already be considered at the peak of its popularity, but Mugen Train ‘s groundbreaking success etched its name into anime history. The film surpassed the long-standing box office records of classics such as Makoto Shinkai’s Your Name and Studio Ghibli’s Spirited Away .

After the release of the Infinity Castle film this year , both Demon Slayer films now rank as the top two among the highest-grossing Japanese films of all time. The film’s success also somewhat influenced Ufotable’s decision to make a trilogy for the Infinity Castle Arc , which turned out for the best. However, Mugen Train ‘s success isn’t only thanks to the flashy animation but also the thrilling fight scenes and emotional weight. The arc was only 13 chapters long in the manga, and yet it completely changed the course of the story.

Rengoku’s Voice Actor Shares His Thoughts on the Best Demon Slayer Moment of All Time

As per Oricon, he shares, “It was a night of fierce battles between Tanjiro and his friends against Enmu, and between Rengoku Kyojuro and Akaza, which was short in time but felt incredibly long. I remember feeling a great sense of responsibility as I recorded, knowing that this one night’s battle would have great significance for Tanjiro and his friends going forward.”

He added, “I’m sure many people, like Tanjiro, were encouraged by the words ‘Burn Your Heart,’ which are also in the title of episode seven. I myself am one of them. I was happy to be able to look back on the time of the Mugen Train with everyone again through the rebroadcast!”

Demon Slayer Still Can’t Top Its First Movie Ever

The fight between Rengoku and Akaza isn’t the best because of the thrilling action or the fight choreography, but because of the impact it had on the overall story . His final words, “Set your heart ablaze,” simply mean having a strong desire to work towards one’s goal even in the face of adversity. His death was a reminder to Tanjiro and the others that they were truly too weak to protect everyone. This is all the more reason why Rengoku’s death sparked a new flame in the three rookie Demon Slayers , who swore to continue moving forward, even if they were sad or filled with regret.

They dedicated themselves to training and strived to become stronger, especially Tanjiro, who didn’t want to let anyone down as he did with Rengoku. Tanjiro carried the guard of Kyojuro’s sword with him as a reminder of his determination and his desire to be like the Flame Hashira. The determination that he gained thanks to Rengoku’s sacrifice stayed with him until the end of the story, shaping his journey going forward.

Do you think Demon Slayer has another fight that has a similar level of emotional impact? Or you can head down to the comments to share your favorite fight in the series.

title: 3 More New Anime to Watch If You Miss 1990s Anime
content:
There’s no denying that the 1990s was a revolutionary decade for the anime industry, as it introduced several iconic films and series that are still loved even now. The animation styles were distinctive, with grainy visuals that can’t be replicated today. The music was unforgettable, and each story had a unique plot to offer, which made these shows and movies even more unforgettable. However, it’s not just the plot or visuals that make these series special, as fans often have an emotional attachment to some of their childhood favorites . It was an era before streaming platforms became popular, but several Japanese anime series were made accessible worldwide thanks to TV channels in English-dubbed formats.

Anime is now a mainstream form of media, pulling in more viewers over the years. Since it’s often overwhelming to find the right anime to start with, many beginners would turn to a series that recently went popular. Unfortunately, a majority of these newer series have a completely different vibe than the 1990s. While the stunning beauty of the 1990s can’t be recreated today , there are plenty of newer series that will remind you of that era. Keep in mind this list doesn’t include reboots of older classics with the same plot but with modern animation.

3) Cyberpunk Edgerunners

The best spooky anime Netflix has to offer is none other than its exclusive Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, based on the popular video game franchise Cyberpunk 2077. The anime captures the perfect sci-fi and spooky vibe of Night City from the game, presenting characters immersed in its most compelling elements. As an original anime, it is exceptionally well-written, with characters’ actions impacting others in ways that are bound to make fans cry as they watch the narrative unfold.

Across just 10 episodes, this anime is scary, dark, emotional, and occasionally funny, making it perfect not just for its spooky elements but also for its overall vibe. However, the biggest reason fans should watch it is that the anime’s second season is arriving on October 20 . While the two seasons aren’t directly connected, as the second will feature its own narrative, watching the first season will reveal what makes this anime so amazing and why it won the Anime of the Year award. With the Netflix exclusive Cyberpunk: Edgerunners returning with a new season this October, there honestly can’t be a better anime to watch on the streaming platform.

2) Love Through a Prism

Set in early 1990s London, the story follows Lili Ichijouin, who traveled all the way from Japan to enroll in the prestigious Saint Thomas Art Academy. However, her parents wouldn’t let her continue her studies if she didn’t rank at the top of her class. Despite the pressure, she tries her best to make her dream of becoming a painter a reality. As she’s driven by her desperation and passion, she meets Kit Church, a gifted student known not only for his talent but also for his detachment from others.

Watching Kit being completely devoted to painting sparks sincerity and resilience in Lili as well, as she tries to perform better. As the two continue to get to know more about each other, they share more than just their love for art. This romantic story puts them through the challenge of breaking free from societal norms and embracing their true selves despite the opposition from everyone around them.

1) Kowloon Generic Romance

Kowloon Generic Romance is the exact opposite of what its title might suggest, combining a romance story with sci-fi mystery elements. The anime was released in 2025 and already had a live-action adaptation debut this year as well. Kowloon Generic Romance boasts a gorgeous, detailed art style that encapsulates the nostalgia of early 2000s romance series, while adding a touch of modernity through the application of subverting tropes at every turn. If you’re into unsettling, mysterious atmospheres combined with relatable characters falling in love, this show is absolutely for you.

The story of Kowloon Generic Romance is set in the high-tech, futuristic Kowloon Walled City. Real estate agents Reiko and Hajime work within the city bounds together and are engaging in the beginnings of an office romance. In the background of this seemingly innocent dynamic, Reiko begins to notice strange peculiarities surrounding her relationship with Hajime that result in her poking around about her past. When Reiko’s reality begins to seem less and less real, she discovers a haunting secret about a past version of herself that seems to have existed before she can remember.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

title: Miss Vinland Saga? New 2027 Anime Confirms Its Release Date & It’s the Next Must-Watch
content:
One of the most anticipated anime of 2027 confirmed its release date in a brand new trailer. Since fans of Vinland Saga fans still have no idea when to expect the anime’s third season, this upcoming historical anime will be perfect for fans to watch in the meantime. Although it’s been almost four years since the second season premiered, the creator confirmed in October that the third season still isn’t under production. Lucky for fans, among the several incredible anime coming next year, Hitoshi Iwaaki’s award-winning manga, Historie , will premiere during the Winter anime lineup of 2027.

2026 is nearing its end, which means that the upcoming series for next year are sharing new information before the year wraps up. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 lineup, as it includes highly anticipated sequels and debuts. Historie is one of the Winter 2027 anime series that you need to watch, especially if you’re a fan of historical Seinen like Vinland Saga. While most international fans are most familiar with the creator because of Parasyte , not many know about his underrated historical manga, Historie . The anime released its key visual and second promotional trailer earlier this week to confirm its release date.

What Is the Release Date of Historie ?

The latest update reveals Historie will premiere on January 8th, 2027. The caption of the second promotional video also reveals the broadcast information, including the schedule for each TV network where the anime will be aired. The anime also reveals that it will be streaming on Amazon Prime Video for Japanese fans starting January 13th, after a few days of delay.

Viewers will require a membership to stream the show online every Wednesday. However, the streaming information is only for Japanese fans, since there hasn’t been any mention of global availability. The anime will likely share the streaming details for outside of Japan at least a few weeks before the premiere. Considering the hype and scale of the project, it’s almost a given that the anime will definitely make its debut on international platforms.

Historie Is a Must-Watch for Vinland Saga Fans

While both stories have different narrative structures , they focus on the survival and epic journey of the protagonists. Not only that, but the themes of resilience and the coming-of-age story in Historie are something that Vinland Saga fans are sure to love. While Thorfinn’s gruesome journey centers around grief, regret, and redemption, Eumenes’s story follows his exceptional story as a brilliant strategist. Written by a legendary creator, Historie is already causing quite a lot of buzz, especially since it has a unique premise.

The manga has been serializing since 2003, and it’s finally getting the attention it deserves. Set in the mid-14th century BC Greece, the story follows a fictionalized account of Eumenes , who later became known throughout the world as the secretary and general of Alexander the Great. Much about Eumenes’ history is a mystery, which is why Hitoshi Iwaaki took creative liberty to tell his version of his story. While Alexander is famous for being one of the greatest military commanders in history, Eumenes’ name is somewhat forgotten by the world.

Are you excited to see Historie bring its exceptional storytelling to anime? Do you think it can live up to the expectations? Let us know in the comments below!

Written by a legendary creator, Historie is already causing quite a lot of buzz, especially since it has a unique premise.

The manga has been serializing since 2003, and it’s finally getting the attention it deserves. Set in the mid-14th century BC Greece, the story follows a fictionalized account of Eumenes , who later became known throughout the world as the secretary and general of Alexander the Great. Much about Eumenes’ history is a mystery, which is why Hitoshi Iwaaki took creative liberty to tell his version of his story. While Alexander is famous for being one of the greatest military commanders in history, Eumenes’ name is somewhat forgotten by the world.
Are you excited to see Historie bring its exceptional storytelling to anime? Do you think it can live up to the expectations? Let us know in the comments below!

title: New Live-Action Hana-Kimi Series Unveils More Cast, New Trailer
content:
The staff for the new live-action television series based on the late Hisaya Nakajo 's classic shōjo manga Hana-Kimi ( Hana Zakari no Kimi-tachi e ) unveiled four more cast members and a new 30-second trailer on Saturday.

The newly announced regular cast member, as well as three cast members for the first four episodes, are:

Miu Arai as Rika Yamashina, Izumi Sano's team manager in junior high school who knows Sano's past

Ryōko Yūi as Io Nanba, Minami Nanba's mother and Umeda's older sister

Yūto Adachi as Shizuki Ashiya, Mizuki's half-brother who dotes on her

Japanese-American track-and-field star Mizuki has gotten herself to transfer to a high school in Japan...but not just any school! To be close to her idol, high jumper Izumi Sano, she's going to an all-guys' high school...and disguising herself as a boy! But as fate would have it, they're more than classmates...they're roommates! Now, Mizuki must keep her secret in the classroom, the locker room, and her own bedroom. And her classmates--and the school nurse--must cope with a new transfer student who may make them question their own orientation...

The television series stars:

• Hana Kawamura as Mizuki Ashiya

• The Rampage member Makoto Hasegawa as Izumi Sano

• The Rampage member Itsuki Fujiwara as Shūichi Nakatsu

• Ryūgūjō member Keigo Itō as Shinji Noe

• Ryūgūjō member Yūki Tomita as Kyōgo Sekime

• Lienel member Miro Takaoka as Taiki Kayashima

• Lienel member Riku Morita as Senri Nakao

• Genosuke as Megumi Tennōji

• Tagright member Daigo Kobayashi as Minami Nanba

• Tagright member Tomoki Nishiyama as Masao Himejima

• Gekidan Exile member Yūki Sakurai as Itsuki Kujō

• Hiroto Takahashi as Makoto Kagurazaka

Keisuke Shibata and NTV 's Shiori Ueno are directing the series, and Fumie Koga , Yuka Arai , and Kazumi Ōki are writing the scripts with composition by Yōko Tamura. Kōji Endō ( Nyaight of the Living Cat , live-action Blade of the Immortal , Terraformars ) is scoring the music.

The 10-member girl group CIRRA is performing a cover of YUI 's "CHE.R.RY" song as the opening theme, and the band Ryūgūjō is performing the ending theme song "Suki Dakara" (Because I Like You).

The half-hour eight-episode series will premiere on the NTV channel on December 5 at 2:30 p.m. (12:30 a.m. EST). The TVer and Hulu services will stream the series in Japan a half hour later, and Hulu will also stream a "director's cut" of the series.

A separate new stage play adaptation will open with most of the series' cast one week after the series ends on February 13-15 in Osaka. It will then travel to Aichi on February 18-19 and Tokyo on March 13-22. Shintarō Sugano is writing and directing the stage play.

The manga inspired an anime adaptation that had its episode 1 world premiere at the Anime NYC event on August 23, 2025. It premiered on the Tokyo MX channel on January 4, 2026 at 9:30 p.m. (7:30 a.m. EST), and it also ran on BS11 , MBS , CBC TV , RKB Mainichi Broadcasting , and other channels. Crunchyroll streamed the anime with English subtitles and same-day dub in North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, the CIS, and India. The anime's second season debuted on July 1.

Hana Zakari no Kimi-tachi e ( Hana-Kimi ) was Nakajo's defining work, running in Hakusensha 's Hana to Yume magazine from 1996 to 2004.

The manga inspired a 2007 live-action television series and a second live-action series starring AKB48 idol group member Atsuko Maeda in 2011. Besides the two Japanese live-action television series, the manga also inspired a live-action television version in South Korea and a 2006 live-action television version in Taiwan.

title: Dragon Ball Super Secretly Has a King of the Saiyans It Hasn’t Even Used Yet
content:
A major aspect that’s yet to get explored in the Dragon Ball multiverse is the only living king of the Saiyans, Universe 6’s Sadala. The Tournament of Power revealed to the Z Fighters that there is an existing Saiyan planet. Goku and Vegeta lost their home world in Universe 7 when Frieza destroyed Planet Vegeta . However, the sister universe to theirs still featured Planet Sandala which is represented by young Saiyan fighters Cabba, Caulifla and Kale.

Cabba reveals himself to be a Saiyan when he meets Goku and Vegeta, and they find out that the planet still very much exists. They learn that the Saiyans are much more peaceful, but still carry a lot of power when called upon in combat. The only teaser that isn’t revealed is who or what King Sadala is. He doesn’t make an on-screen appearance, so no one knows what he looks like, how powerful he is or how he rules. The statements from everyone else make it sound like a peaceful existence, but everything isn’t always what it seems in the alternate universes either. There’s still a lot left to answer.

Is Sadala His Own Ruler Or More Like King Vegeta?

A funny “got you” moment from Dragon Ball Super is when the Z Fighters find out who Frost is. They see him as the morally good alternate to Frieza initially . However, it’s all an elaborate ruse, as he’s actually a double agent of sorts that could care less about others and is just out for himself. Could Sadala be the same? Now, the Saiyans from Universe 6 have already laid the groundwork for being good individuals, but their home world might have secrets they don’t even know. King Sadala might mirror King Vegeta more than they think.

Nevertheless, in all likelihood, he could just as easily be a good king that treats his subordinates with respect. Would his powerful ability match his Saiyan brethren from another universe? He’s got a lot to match up to from Universe 7. King Vegeta proved a powerful Saiyan in his lifetime. The war-torn Saiyans built up their strength through attrition over the years as war never stopped while working for Frieza. Sadala and the Universe 6 Saiyans live in peace, so would he carry the similar strength to his royal counterpart? Knowing Goku and Vegeta, it’s likely they’ll want to find out that answer.

Universe 6 Saiyans Show Rage Is Alive

The newest Saiyans proved one element similar to the originals, and that’s activating their rage to become Super Saiyans. This lone facet tells the fans a lot about Sadala. The planet isn’t full of friendly pacifists. They’re ready to step up and fight. The lone remaining king of the Saiyans clearly didn’t send Cabba, Caulifla and Kale to the Tournament of Power with just well wishes .

Cabba, specifically as a member of the Sadala Defense Forces, displays what the expectations are to defend his planet. King Sadala doesn’t want fake tough guys in the fight. They seem to match what he wants in a soldier, which likely tells the audience that Sadala is a Super Saiyan too. There’s a lot left to unpack in this particular arc. However, there’s little doubt that it won’t get addressed at some point.

It’s the last remaining Saiyan planet in existence, and Vegeta and Goku would want to see the planet and its king soon. What do you think King Sadala will be like if Dragon Ball Super ever introduces him? Let us know in the comments.

title: Precure Franchise Announces FUNtasic Precure! Anime
content:
Toei Animation announced on Thursday that the 24th entry in the Precure franchise has the title FUNtasic Precure!

The tagline for the anime is "Shine! Everyone's smiles! Welcome to the FUNtasic party!" The logo features party motifs such as confetti poppers and garlands.

The company also announced in October that the Precure franchise will receive a television anime spinoff titled Dual Shadow ~Precure Villain Heroines~ which will premiere next year.

The Star Detective Precure! anime, the 23rd and latest main television anime in the franchise, debuted on February 1. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime in North America, Central America, South America, Australia, New Zealand, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and CIS.

Eiga Meitantei Precure! Fushigi na Niwa to Futari no Himitsu ( Star Detective Precure! The Movie: The Mysterious Garden and the Secret of 2 People) — the film for Star Detective Precure! — opened in Japan on September 18, and ranked at #3 in its opening weekend. The film sold 358,000 tickets to earn 446 million yen (about US$2.82 million) in its first three days.

Toei Animation recently produced two 20th anniversary projects for the franchise. The Power of Hope: Precure Full Bloom television anime debuted in October 2023, and was a sequel to Yes! Precure 5 featuring the cast as adults. Mahō Tsukai Precure!!: MIRAI DAYS debuted in January 2025, and was a sequel to Witchy Pretty Cure!

Upate: Spelling of FUNtasic corrected. Thanks, MarthKoopa and EmeraldSaucer.

title: Major Shojo Anime Breakout Confirms Season 2 Return With First Look
content:
Shojo anime continues to dominate upcoming seasonal anime rotations , with breakout hits like Firefly Wedding becoming viral sensations, as well as fans spinning rumors regarding which new series will be getting a sequel first. Luckily for many, Tamon’s B-side , a new shojo anime that originally debuted in December 2025 is finally returning with a second season sometime in the future. Following a live fan event in Tokyo called F/ACE FIRST LIVE “NAUTICAL STAR,” it was officially announced that the idol-centric will finally be coming back, with the show’s official X (formerly Twitter) uploading a short teaser trailer to share the news.

While there have been no dates given regarding when fans will be able to hear additional details or when the second season will release , it’s likely that the same production team from J.C.STAFF that worked on Tamon’s B-Side Season 1 will be returning. Season 1 was directed by Chika Nagaoka, best known for her previous work on Case Closed , with series composition and scripts from Chiaki Nagai who previously worked on Horimiya , another massive romance series. Check out the announcement teaser below.

Tamon’s B-side Is the Gold Standard Romance For a Niche Shojo Trope

Tamon’s B-side explores an extremely popular but surprisingly niche ship dynamic between two characters, focusing entirely on the budding romantic relationship between an idol and their “stan” — a slang term used to describe an extremely enthusiastic and dedicated fan to a person, character, or piece of media. The anime follows a high school-aged housekeeper named Utage Kinoshita who started working part-time to help fund her love for F/ACE, her favorite idol group. While working, she stumbles into a situation where she discovers that her favorite member of the group, Tamon Fukuhara, whose stage persona is boisterous and confident, is actually extremely timid and prone to spiraling into dramatic episodes fueled by his own self doubt.

The series immediately became a hit with shojo fans in part because of the anime’s gorgeous animation which turned each member of F/ACE into a bishonen dream as well as its earnest humor and genuinely adorable romance between Utage and Tamon. The pair’s relationship develops gradually throughout the first season with Utage working as his personal housekeeper. Instead of her interest in the idol waning because of his “real self,” she instead becomes an anchor to help support him in his day-to-day life both on and off stage. The premise for Tamon’s B-side feels like something plucked directly from an old school boy band fan fiction and lands perfectly every single episode.

Where To Read and Watch Tamon’s B-side

Based on an original manga written by Yuki Shiwasu, Tamon’s B-side began publishing in the famous shojo magazine Hana to Yume in 2021. The series is still ongoing, and as of writing, currently has seventeen collected volumes in print. Viz Media publishes the manga in English and currently has thirteen volumes available in both print and digital. While there’s still no confirmation when new details regarding the second season of Tamon’s B-side will release, it’s likely to begin adapting Rintaro’s story arc which reveals the true personality of one of F/ACE’s other members.

The first season of Tamon’s B-side released in December 2025, running for thirteen episodes which adapted the first 33-chapters of the manga. Crunchyroll picked up and currently hosts the anime adaptation on their streaming service for global audiences. When the anime initially began airing, the manga had roughly 1.75-million copies in circulation which jumped to 3.5-million by the time the first season came to an end.

Tamon’s B-side has been nominated for multiple manga awards in that time as well, and as of writing is still publishing new chapters, meaning that there’s still plenty more of Utage and Tamon for fans of the series to look forward to in the future. Are you excited for Season 2? Let us know in the comments!

title: Netflix’s Darkest Sci-Fi Anime of 2026 Is Already a Masterpiece Worthy of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
content:
Netflix has released a new dark sci-fi anime with all 12 episodes worthy of replacing Cyberpunk: Edgerunners for your Thanksgiving weekend binge. As an original anime series on Netflix, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners delivers a grim story with social inequality as its central driving force. Both seasons explore this notion through different sets of characters as they navigate the neon-lit streets of Night City, amplified by thrilling sci-fi action. If these are the elements that made you love Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , then Fool Night , with all its episodes already available on Netflix , is here to become a worthy replacement for the anime.

Based on the manga of the same name, the anime is set in a distant future where thick clouds have covered the entire Earth, plunging the world into darkness and cold. With plants naturally dying out, the lack of oxygen continues to increase. Humanity’s solution is a procedure called Transfloration, which plants seeds inside people nearing death and transforms them into Spiriflors, plants capable of producing oxygen. This fresh concept is further elevated by a botanical horror premise mixed with crime thriller elements unfolding in this dark world.

Netflix’s Fool Night Is 2026’s Most Brilliant Sci-Fi Anime

The heart of the series is its main character, Toshiro Kamiya, a broke young man who, after a particularly bad night, undergoes the Transfloration process, primarily because he wants the 10 million yen that would allow him to spend the rest of his life eating good food and living happily. However, things don’t go as planned, as his money is stolen after the procedure. Nevertheless, Toshiro develops a strange ability to communicate with Spiriflors. This leads him to join a facility investigating the numerous crimes related to Spiriflors, turning the series into a crime thriller in which Toshiro uses his ability to solve various plant-based crimes.

With this foundation, the series begins unveiling the motives behind the various crimes, with each one feeling more human than the last. Meanwhile, the series also follows Toshiro as he takes on duties helping people who want to communicate with the Spiriflors who were once close to them. The result is an emotionally complex exploration of human nature and the motives behind people transforming into plant-like beings, revealing how the grim trade-offs can stem from the most unimaginable circumstances. All the while, the series explores Toshiro’s own complicated situation with his mother, which, from the very beginning, makes viewers emotionally invested in him and eager to see him live the remainder of his life to the fullest.

On top of this brilliant premise, the anime is also gorgeously crafted by Sunrise and Shaft, elevating the botanical elements of the series and presenting them exactly as they are meant to feel. This makes the anime one of the most visually appealing series of 2026 as well. All in all, Netflix’s Fool Night is a true sci-fi masterpiece that deserves to stand alongside other masterpieces on the platform, such as Cyberpunk: Edgerunners .

What do you think about Fool Night as the best dark sci-fi anime of 2026 on Netflix? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

All the while, the series explores Toshiro’s own complicated situation with his mother, which, from the very beginning, makes viewers emotionally invested in him and eager to see him live the remainder of his life to the fullest.

On top of this brilliant premise, the anime is also gorgeously crafted by Sunrise and Shaft, elevating the botanical elements of the series and presenting them exactly as they are meant to feel. This makes the anime one of the most visually appealing series of 2026 as well. All in all, Netflix’s Fool Night is a true sci-fi masterpiece that deserves to stand alongside other masterpieces on the platform, such as Cyberpunk: Edgerunners .
